introduction: At this level, we cover the most important international boundaries of India. The names of these lines, the individuals who drew them, and the countries they separate are the most frequently tested facts in basic exams.

core_concepts.title: Radcliffe Line
core_concepts.description:
Countries: **India & Pakistan** (and India & Bangladesh). 
History: It was demarcated by Sir Cyril Radcliffe during the partition of India in 1947. (Since East Pakistan became Bangladesh, the India-Bangladesh border is also technically part of the Radcliffe Line).

core_concepts.title: McMahon Line
core_concepts.description:
Countries: **India & China** (Specifically the Arunachal Pradesh sector). 
History: It was negotiated by Sir Henry McMahon at the 1914 Shimla Convention. China officially disputes and does not recognize this line.

core_concepts.title: Durand Line
core_concepts.description:
Countries: Currently between **Pakistan & Afghanistan**. 
History: Drawn by Sir Mortimer Durand in 1893 between British India and the Emirate of Afghanistan. After partition, it became the border between Pakistan and Afghanistan (though a tiny 106 km stretch of Pakistan Occupied Kashmir technically touches Afghanistan).

core_concepts.title: Palk Strait
core_concepts.description:
Countries: **India & Sri Lanka**. 
Key Feature: It is a maritime boundary (strait) that separates the state of Tamil Nadu (India) from the Jaffna District of northern Sri Lanka. The Gulf of Mannar is located just south of it.

important_entities.name: Longest International Border
important_entities.significance: A very common exam question: 'With which country does India share its longest international border?' Answer: Bangladesh. (The shortest is with Afghanistan - 106 km).

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Exam Trap: Students often associate the Durand Line with India and Afghanistan. Technically, about 106 km of POK borders Afghanistan (which India claims as its own), but practically and majorly, the Durand line today serves as the border between **Pakistan and Afghanistan**.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation:
Length of borders from longest to shortest: 
Ba = Bangladesh, Ch = China, Pa = Pakistan, N = Nepal. 
M = Myanmar, B = Bhutan, A = Afghanistan.

exam_strategy_tips: A patent SSC CHSL/MTS question: 'The boundary line between India and China is known as?' Answer: McMahon Line.
